pattern_explanation: Some Polish and English words look almost identical because they come from the same Latin or Greek roots, but their meanings have drifted apart over time. Learners tend to assume the shared form carries the same sense, so the trap lies in the meaning rather than in the spelling.
false_friend_warning: Beware of false friends: the Polish adjective transliterated as aktualny means current or up to date, not actual, and the one transliterated as konkretny means specific, not concrete, so learners should not match them by their similar English forms.
